text:
jane_acme: Hey team — our private VPC deployment to Redwood started failing around 11:12 UTC. Streaming responses drop with TLS errors and curl shows "SSL: certificate subject name '---' does not match" sometimes. We didn't change configs. Help?

alice_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact curl output (redact tokens)? Also which private deployment: VPC or on-prem, and region?

jane_acme: It's our VPC deployment in us-west-2. Repro steps: `curl -v https://api.redwood.run/v1/streams -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT"` — output: `* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* SSL: certificate subject name 'redwood-prod' does not match 'api.redwood.run'
* Closing connection 0`

brian_sre: Ok a couple of hypotheses: 1) corporate TLS inspection / SSL proxy rewriting certs, 2) NAT / ephemeral port/NACL asymmetry causing handshakes to reset mid-stream, or 3) DNS returning an internal IP (split-horizon) with a mismatched cert.

maria_eng: Can you run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.run:443 -servername api.redwood.run -showcerts` from a host in that VPC and paste the first certificate subject/CN? Also `dig +short api.redwood.run` and `curl -vk --resolve api.redwood.run:443:34.120.22.11 https://api.redwood.run/` (replace IP with resolved redwood IP) — that will help tell if it's DNS vs TLS MITM.

jane_acme: Ran openssl — cert CN is `corp-proxy.local` and issuer is our corp CA. So looks like MITM. But weird: only streaming endpoints fail; plain non-streaming generation calls usually succeed.

alice_support: Streaming uses long-lived connections + server push / chunked transfer. TLS MITM often breaks HTTP/2 framing or rewrites certs causing client libs to reject when they verify SNI. Two immediate checks: ensure your egress allowlist includes SNI/domain exceptions for `api.redwood.run` and `*.redwood.run`, and that your proxy allows TLS passthrough for our endpoints.

brian_sre: Also check your SG/NACL: outbound 443 to our IPs must be allowed and ephemeral port range allowed inbound from NAT. On AWS: NACLs are stateless — you must permit ephemeral port range 1024-65535 both directions (or the range your NAT uses). Example NACL rule pairs: `ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0` (outbound) and `ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0` (inbound). If NACL blocks return ephemeral ports, you'll see mid-connection resets.

jane_acme: Our NACLs currently only allow ephemeral 32768-65535. Could that explain intermittent behavior?

maria_eng: Yes — if NAT selects a source port lower than 32768 you'll get drops. Try widening to 1024-65535 or adjust your NAT ephemeral port range. Also verify your NAT health checks (some NGWs probe 443 frequently and can trigger state issues).

alice_support: Another quick repro: from a VPC host try `curl -v --no-keepalive https://api.redwood.run/v1/` and then `curl -v --keepalive https://api.redwood.run/v1/stream` to compare. If keepalive/long connections break but short ones succeed that's a strong signal for NACL/conntrack issues or TLS inspection timeouts.

jane_acme: I ran both. Short calls OK, streaming with keepalive fails after ~30s. We do have an inline proxy that terminates TLS and reissues certs; can we get a compatibility note?

maria_eng: Short answer: streaming requires true TLS passthrough (no re-termination) or a proxy that preserves SNI and does full end-to-end cert verification without rewriting the CN. If your proxy reissues certs you must configure clients to trust the proxy cert (not recommended) or set proxy to SNI passthrough for `api.redwood.run`.

brian_sre: From infra side, checklist for your network team:
- Verify DNS from VPC: `dig +short api.redwood.run` (expect public Redwood IPs).
- Check NACL pairs allow ephemeral ports both ways (1024-65535 recommended).
- Ensure SG outbound allows 443 to Redwood IPs; SG inbound for ephemeral ports from NAT/IGW as needed.
- If using proxy: configure TLS passthrough for streaming endpoints or add SNI allowlist for `api.redwood.run`.
- Collect a packet capture around a failed stream (tcpdump -w) and upload so we can inspect RSTs.

jane_acme: Sharing outputs: dig -> `34.120.22.11`. We've widened NACL to 1024-65535 and set proxy to passthrough for `api.redwood.run`. Retesting now...

deploy-bot: [deployment] Canary rule updated for acme-vpc: NACL widened, proxy passthrough flag toggled.

jane_acme: After changes, streaming is stable. Thanks!

alice_support: Great — leaving notes here for others: common root causes for streaming TLS failures from private VPCs: TLS inspection re-signing, NACL ephemeral port truncation, split-horizon DNS pointing at internal proxies, and aggressive conntrack timeouts on NAT appliances.

maria_eng: I'll open an internal KB linking to our streaming compatibility checklist and example NACL/SG templates. :memo:

brian_sre: Marking this resolved unless you see recurrence.

jane_acme: All good for now, will ping if it happens again. :thumbsup:
